newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee higher as dollar weakens overseas.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee higher as dollar weakens overseas.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed higher against the dollar on Friday, mainly on the U.S. currency's drop against major currencies, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 59.23 to the dollar after opening at 59.30, the same as its closing price on Thursday.
The central bank fixed buying and selling at 58.2194 and 59.3956, respectively .
The rupee was untraded in early trade as sellers, sensing a desire by the central bank to push down the local currency, refused to part with dollar plus positions, dealers said.

"But after seeing the dollar weakening against international currencies today, people realised the central bank could not continue to be positive towards the dollar," a Standard Chartered Bank dealer said.
"Realising that the central bank will push the dollar down or at least keep it unchanged, some banks began selling, which brought the greenback down," a local bank dealer said.
Overnight call money, which opened at 9.50 percent, closed at 10 percent with the market liquid, dealers said.
